title: Mvouni university students strike and demonstrate over student conditions
location: University of the Comoros, Mvouni campus, Grande Comore
organizer: University students; no formal organizer identified in the reviewed accounts.
threshold_50_evidence: No report gives the number of people at the 2 January campus action. Search-result reports call it a demonstration, but the university’s roughly 6,000 students are enrollment context, not attendance.

title.summary: The opened MasiwaKomor article confirms a 2 January strike; search results from Eurecanews and Al-Fajr call the campus action a demonstration.

start_date.summary: MasiwaKomor dates the strike to Monday 2 January 2023; search-only reports also date the Mvouni demonstration to that Monday.

location.summary: Reports place the action at the University of the Comoros’ Mvouni campus.

organizer.summary: Students took the action; neither opened report identifies a formal organizer.

demands.summary: Reports describe student representation and health-mutual governance, registration/exam access and campus conditions. The political-behavior/process category is used only for the student-representation demand.

participants_original.summary: No attendee count is reported. S010’s roughly 6,000 students paying fees is university enrollment, not protest attendance.

participants_min.summary: No numerical lower bound is supported.

participants_max.summary: No numerical upper bound is supported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The campus demonstration is reported, but no count or clear qualitative estimate establishes 50 participants.

end_date.summary: S002 says tensions eased from 3 January; S010 describes a renewed dispute and delegations on 9 January. Neither establishes when the physical 2 January action ended.

protester_violence.summary: S002 rejects a separate claim that students demonstrated in the street and were beaten or gassed; it does not establish whether violence occurred during the campus action, so this remains unknown.

state_response.summary: University measures and later student delegations/ministerial discussions are reported, but a response attributable to the 2 January action under the event-level categories is not established.

notes: The candidate is the reported 2 January campus action. S010 describes a distinct 9 January escalation, a gendarmerie visit and a ministry delegation during the same dispute, but does not establish a second public assembly. Keep those later negotiations as campaign context pending episode review. Do not use the university enrollment figure as attendance. S002 and S010 are reports from the same outlet/author, not independent corroboration.
open_questions: Was a public group of at least 50 present on 2 January?
Did the 9 January escalation include a separate public assembly or only delegations and negotiations?
When did the physical 2 January action end?
Does the state-university/ministerial target meet the original state-policy rule for each demand?

title: Volo Volo market sellers protest Moroni municipal fee changes
location: Volo Volo market and outside Moroni city hall, Moroni, Grande Comore
organizer: Market sellers, including women vendors; no formal organization is named.
threshold_50_evidence: S006 says women sellers gathered outside city hall while sellers stopped trading, but gives no attendance estimate. Do not convert the market-wide work stoppage, vendor population, tables, or duration into assembly attendance.

title.summary: S006’s opened article reports sellers opposing Moroni municipal market-fee changes; the January archive listing also surfaces the 30 January strike.

start_date.summary: S006 dates the sellers’ action to Monday 30 January 2023.

location.summary: S006 places the work stoppage at Volo Volo market and women sellers’ gathering outside Moroni city hall.

organizer.summary: S006 identifies sellers/women vendors but names no formal organization.

demands.summary: Sellers objected to municipal changes in how market-space fees were assessed and paid; coded as price/tax policy.

participants_min.summary: No numerical lower bound is supported.

participants_max.summary: No numerical upper bound is supported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: A gathering outside city hall is reported, but its size is not quantified or qualitatively established as at least 50.

end_date.summary: The market stoppage lasted almost the whole day; the article does not establish the gathering’s physical end.

protester_violence.summary: No event-specific evidence establishes protester violence or its absence.

state_response.summary: A municipal representative held a press point, but the record does not show accommodation or another coded response to the gathering.

notes: S006 reports sellers stopped trading for almost the whole day and women sellers gathered outside city hall. Sellers’ fee account differs from the municipal representative’s explanation. S008 reports a municipal press conference on 30 January about unregistered market tables and alleged diverted revenue; it does not report the seller gathering and is not independent evidence that it occurred. Do not use counts of tables, sellers affected, or hours of stoppage as participants.
open_questions: Was the city-hall gathering at least 50 people?
How long did the public gathering itself last?
What were the applicable fee rules and how did they change?
Did the municipal press point respond to the gathering or address a separate municipal investigation?

title: Mutsamudu port truck drivers strike in support of occasional dockworkers
organizer: Dockworkers and truck drivers acting in solidarity; the report names a port-workers’ union secretary but does not identify a formal initiating body.
threshold_50_evidence: The 1 February issue says the strike had lasted about 20 days but gives no count of striking dockers or truck drivers and describes no public gathering. “More than 35 of 75 dockers recruited” is a staffing figure, not attendance.

title.summary: The 1 February Gazette issue reports a truck-driver strike in solidarity with dockworkers at Mutsamudu port.

start_date.summary: The issue says the strike had been underway for 20 days as of 1 February; January is therefore assigned only at month precision, with no exact start date inferred.

location.summary: The article places the strike at the port of Mutsamudu, Anjouan.

organizer.summary: Dockworkers and truck drivers are described in solidarity; the union and initiating organizer are not fully identified.

demands.summary: Dockers reportedly sought a different employment status, salary, daily compensation and health coverage; the article also quotes truckers calling on the government and the port company to find a solution. State-policy relationship remains unresolved.

participants_original.summary: No strike participant count is reported.

participants_min.summary: No numerical lower bound is supported; 35/75 are not attendance.

participants_max.summary: No numerical upper bound is supported; no truck-driver count is supplied.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No count of participants or evidence of a gathering of 50 or more; work stoppage and port inactivity are not attendance.

end_date.summary: The strike was still described as continuing on 1 February; no physical end date is reported.

protester_violence.summary: The selected report does not establish protester violence or its absence.

state_response.summary: The article says a delegation from Moroni would begin discussions; this is prospective, not evidence that talks occurred or that demands were accommodated.

notes: This is a labor-action lead, not a verified mass assembly. The May 2015 codebook excludes company-specific labor negotiations unless the action becomes a public event, such as a march or a demand on government; the article’s trucker quote addresses government, but does not establish the state-policy connection, public format, or 50-person threshold. The 20-day duration is approximate and the issue is dated 1 February, so only January start month is supported. No February source closing the strike was located.
open_questions: Was this a public event involving 50 or more people, rather than only a workplace stoppage?
Were the disputed terms governed by state policy or a state-controlled employer?
What were the actual strike start and end dates?
Did the planned Moroni delegation meet the workers?

title: Opposition Front press conference in Iconi calling for election rules and a boycott
scope: local press conference; any wider mobilization is unverified
organizer: Front commun de l’opposition, as reported in a search result; original source attribution is unresolved.
threshold_50_evidence: The search-result report calls it a press conference but gives no attendee count or evidence of a 50-person public gathering.

title.summary: The search-only Habariza result and Comores Infos archive list an opposition-front statement about boycotting the 2024 presidential election unless common rules were set.

start_date.summary: Habariza’s search result says the press conference took place on 26 January 2023; article publication was 30 January.

location.summary: Habariza’s search result places the press conference in Iconi.

organizer.summary: The search result attributes the conference to the Front commun de l’opposition; “©CMM” origin/ownership is unresolved.

demands.summary: The reported statement called for common election rules and a boycott of the 2024 vote; coded as political behavior/process, not support for a candidate.

participants_original.summary: No attendance number is supplied in the search result or archive listing.

participants_min.summary: No numerical lower bound is supported.

participants_max.summary: No numerical upper bound is supported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: A press conference is reported, but public format and attendance of 50 or more are unverified.

end_date.summary: Only the conference date is reported; its end is not.

protester_violence.summary: No event-specific evidence establishes protester violence or its absence.

state_response.summary: No event-specific government response is reported in the search-only evidence.

notes: Retain as a lead only. The codebook excludes political rallies, while the available search result describes a press conference; it does not establish a public rally or 50 attendees. The article is search-only and carries “©CMM”; no body was opened because origin/ownership remains unresolved. The Comores Infos archive is a separate listing, not independent confirmation of the conference details.
open_questions: Was this a public assembly of 50 or more people, or a press briefing?
Would the event fall under the original exclusion for political rallies?
What is the original CMM story/source and are the two outlets independent?
Was a government response reported elsewhere?
